name: Post Doctoral Fellowship To Women Candidates
briefDescription: UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship for Women Candidates gives unemployed women PhD holders a fellowship of ₹38,800/month (JRF level) or ₹45,000/month (after 2 years, SRF level) for up to 5 years, to support independent post-doctoral research.
descriptionMd:
The UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship for Women Candidates, run by the University Grants Commission (UGC) under the Ministry of Education, supports women who hold a PhD and wish to continue academic research but have not yet been able to secure a university or research position. The fellowship provides a regular income and contingency grant for up to five years, enabling them to publish and build a research career.

Applications are invited once a year through national newspaper advertisements and the UGC website.
benefitsMd:
- **Fellowship stipend:** ₹38,800/month for the first two years (JRF equivalent); ₹45,000/month from year 3 onwards (SRF equivalent), subject to positive annual performance review.
- **Contingency grant:** ₹20,000/year for the first two years; ₹25,000/year from year 3 (for books, journals, lab consumables, field work, etc.).
- **Duration:** up to **5 years** (non-extendable, with annual performance review).
- The fellow is hosted at a **UGC-recognised university or research institution** of their choice.
eligibilityMd:
- Must be a **woman** candidate.
- Must hold a **PhD degree** (provisional certificate accepted if the degree is not yet formally awarded).
- Must be **unemployed** — not holding any regular salaried position at the time of application.
- **Maximum age: 55 years** at the time of application.
- The research proposal must be in a discipline supported by UGC.
exclusionsMd:
- Women who are already employed (regular, contractual, or ad-hoc) are **not eligible**.
- The fellowship is **not renewable** beyond 5 years and cannot be held concurrently with any other fellowship or scholarship.
applicationMd:
Applications are invited once a year through national newspaper advertisements and the UGC website:

**Step 1:** Watch for the annual notification on [ugc.gov.in](https://www.ugc.gov.in/) or in Employment News.
**Step 2:** Download the application form from the UGC website and read the instructions carefully.
**Step 3:** Prepare your **Research Proposal** (typically 2,000–3,000 words) in the prescribed format.
**Step 4:** Arrange a **sponsoring institution** — a UGC-recognised university or research centre willing to host the fellowship.
**Step 5:** Obtain endorsement from the Head of the Department and the Registrar of the host institution.
**Step 6:** Submit the completed application form with all attachments (PhD certificate, endorsements, research proposal, proof of unemployment) to the UGC address / online portal as specified in the notification.
